subject: Data Engineering
title: Z-Ordering and Data Clustering
description: A quick, practical guide to Z-Ordering and Data Clustering.

hook.text: A query filters by customer_id and date. The data is scattered across 1,000 files. Can we do better?

buildup.text: Z-ordering physically co-locates related data in the same files based on specified columns.

discovery.text: After z-ordering by customer_id, a query for one customer reads 5 files instead of 1,000.

twist.text: Z-ordering is expensive — it rewrites the entire table. But the query speed gains can be 10x to 100x.

climax.text: Choose z-order columns based on your most frequent query filters. The right choice transforms performance.

punchline.text: Put related data together. Skip everything else.

quiz.question: What does z-ordering achieve in a lakehouse?
options: Co-locates related data in the same files for faster filtered queries
